title: Company-wide policies & processes — Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Marissa Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees, hiring managers, and operational partners. Where a topic references a specialized runbook or security checklist, the link is included in Related pages.

Scope and ownership

- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to company systems or data.
- Primary owners: People Ops (policy maintenance), Finance (procurement & expenses), Security (access controls & vendor security), Legal (contracts).
- Escalation: For ambiguous cases, raise to People Ops and Security; for procurement disputes escalate to Finance Director.

1) Access & permissions

Principles
- Least privilege: users get the minimum permissions needed to perform their role.
- Role-based access: permissions are primarily granted via role/group assignments in our identity provider (IdP).
- Time-bound access: temporary elevated access for tasks must include an expiration.
- Full MFA and SSO required for all employee accounts.

Key roles and ownership
- Identity & Access Management (IAM) Owner: Security team.
- Request intake and approvals: Hiring manager/Team lead + System owner.
- Audit and periodic review: Security & People Ops (quarterly).

Access request procedure (standard)
1. Submit request via Access Request form (Confluence template /forms/access-request). Include justification, required resources, and duration.
2. Manager approval (email or Slack confirmation).
3. System owner approval (if required for higher privilege).
4. Security review if the request touches regulated or sensitive data.
5. IAM team implements and tags the request with request-id.
6. Auto-expiry is set; follow-up review before any extension.

Emergency access (break glass)
- Use the emergency access process: request via on-call portal, require two approvers (Team lead + Security on-call), log actions in the incident tracker. All emergency access is audited and reviewed post-event.

Periodic reviews
- Quarterly entitlement review: teams receive a report and must certify access lists. Failure to certify triggers access suspension for unverified accounts.

2) Change management

Change categories
- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk (e.g., routine config updates).
- Normal changes: scheduled, require change ticket and approvals.
- Emergency changes: unplanned changes required to restore service or address security incidents.

Change advisory board (CAB)
- Membership: Engineering leads, Security, Product Ops, SRE, and a Finance representative for cost-impacting changes.
- Cadence: weekly for standard/normal change review; emergency CAB convened ad-hoc.

Required artifacts for a Normal change
- Change request ticket (Jira ID).
- Rollout plan with start/end time, rollback criteria, and automated smoke tests.
- Impact assessment and service owner sign-off.
- Communication plan and status channel for stakeholders.

Emergency change procedure
1. Triage and document the incident in the incident tracker.
2. Secure approvals from on-call SRE and Security on-call (phone/SMS + ticket).
3. Execute change with continuous logging and monitoring.
4. Post-change review within 72 hours; follow-up with full RCA if outage or data impact occurred.

Rollback playbook (required in all normal & emergency changes)
- Define explicit rollback steps and automated test verification.
- Identify post-rollback validation and stakeholder notification steps.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Standard change window: Mon–Fri 02:00–06:00 UTC for non-critical services.
- Blackout windows: major product release launches and financial close periods (Finance will publish dates).

3) Data management

Data classification model
- Public: information approved for external publication.
- Internal: non-sensitive company information for employee access.
- Confidential: business-sensitive information (contracts, roadmaps, non-public metrics).
- Regulated: PII, PHI, or any data subject to compliance regimes (GDPR, SOC2, HIPAA).

Handling rules
- Encryption: All Confidential and Regulated data must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Access logging: access to Confidential and Regulated data must be logged and retained for a minimum of 90 days; retention subject to legal requirements.
- Data minimization: systems should store only the data necessary for the stated business purpose.
- Backups: nightly encrypted backups for regulated datasets; test restores quarterly.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: 3 years for Internal data, 7 years for Finance/contractual records, variable for Regulated based on legal requirements.
- Deletion requests: submit Data Deletion Request form; Security and Data Steward approve before execution.

Data transfer & third parties
- Export controls: cross-region transfer of Regulated data requires Security and Legal approval and a documented data flow map.
- Vendor data processing agreement (DPA) required for vendors handling Regulated data.

4) Procurement & expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals
| Amount (USD) | Approval required |
|--------------|------------------|
| <$1,000      | Team lead        |
| $1,000–$25,000 | Department head + Finance reviewer |
| >$25,000     | VP-level + Finance Director + Legal (if contractual) |

Procurement workflow (high-level)
1. Fill Purchase Request (Confluence template /forms/purchase-request) with cost center and justification.
2. Finance validates budget and coding.
3. Contracts team (Legal) reviews vendor agreement for engagements > $25k or those involving data access.
4. Purchase Order (PO) or Corporate Card use per policy.
5. Finance issues PO and tracks invoice payments (Net 30 by default unless negotiated).

Corporate card & employee expenses
- Corporate card issuance managed by Finance; eligibility: managers and members of ops/finance as needed.
- Expense reimbursement: submit receipts within 30 days via Expense system. Per diem and meal caps apply (see Travel section).
- Non-compliant expenses (personal charges, alcohol without approval) will be rejected.

Travel & entertainment expense caps
| Item | Cap (USD) |
|------|-----------|
| Domestic meals (per day) | $75 |
| International meals (per day) | $100 |
| Hotel (standard) | Market rate; upgrades require approval |
| Airfare | Economy unless 8+ hour flight and approved |

5) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist
- Business case and owner identified.
- Security questionnaire completed (vendor self-assessment + SOC2/ISO certs where available).
- DPA and Master Services Agreement (MSA) signed if vendor will process Regulated data.
- Procurement and Finance approvals obtained.
- Onboarding completed in Vendor Registry with assigned owner and contract end date.

Security and SLA expectations
- Vendors with access to Confidential/Regulated data must pass a Security Assessment and provide relevant compliance evidence.
- SLAs should include uptime targets, incident notification windows (72 hours for data breaches, with immediate notification for confirmed exfiltration), and escalation contacts.

Renewal and offboarding
- Renewal checklist 90 days before contract end: review usage, security posture, cost, and alternatives.
- Offboarding: revoke credentials, remove integrations, perform data deletion or return per DPA, and update Vendor Registry.

6) Travel policy (business travel)

Booking and approvals
- All business travel must use the company travel booking tool or approved travel agency.
- Submit Travel Request form at least 10 business days prior for international travel and 5 days for domestic.
- Approvals: Manager + Finance (if > $2,000) + Security review for travel to high-risk regions.

Per diems, lodging, and safety
- Per diem and meal caps listed in Procurement section apply.
- Employees traveling internationally must register travel with Security, carry emergency contact information, and complete the International Travel Safety checklist.
- For travel to high-risk locations, Security will provide a travel brief and may require additional approvals or restrictions.

Travel expenses and reimbursements
- Submit receipts in the Expense system within 30 days. Lost receipts must be reported and require manager justification.
- Limits on alcohol reimbursement: business meals may include a reasonable amount of alcohol but should be itemized and approved.

7) Internal templates and forms

Common templates (location: Confluence /forms)
| Template name | Purpose |
|---------------|---------|
| Access Request | Request access to systems and resources |
| Purchase Request | Initiate procurement and PO requests |
| Travel Request | Business travel approvals and risk review |
| Data Deletion Request | Request deletion or removal of data from systems |
| Vendor Security Questionnaire | Vendor security self-assessment template |
| Change Request | Standard change ticket template with rollback plan |

How to request a new template
1. Create a draft page under /confluence/policies-and-process/templates-draft.
2. Notify People Ops and the relevant owner team for review.
3. After 2 reviewers sign off, People Ops publishes the template to /forms and adds to the templates index.

Audit, compliance, and reporting
- Quarterly reviews: People Ops + Security + Finance run cross-checks for procurement spend, vendor compliance, and access certifications.
- Annual external audit preparation: Security and Finance maintain evidence and run pre-audit checks 90 days before audit window.
- Reporting: incidents, access violations, and policy exceptions are reported via the Incident Response process and triaged within 48 hours.

Exceptions and change control
- Policy exceptions require a documented exception form and approvals from the owning teams (People Ops + Security + Finance depending on scope). Exceptions are time-boxed (max 6 months) and reviewed quarterly.
